question: Nayanars saints were devoted to which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shiva.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Nayanars were a group of 63 Tamil saint-poets of the Bhakti movement who were devoted to Lord Shiva (शिव).

• They flourished in Tamil Nadu roughly between the 6th and 10th centuries CE and composed devotional hymns in Tamil.

• Their counterparts, the Alvars, were devoted to Lord Vishnu; together they led the Bhakti movement in South India.

• Their hymns were later compiled in the Tirumurai, and Sekkizhar's Periya Puranam narrates their lives.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Prominent Nayanars include Appar, Sambandar, Sundarar and Manikkavachakar.

• The Bhakti movement stressed personal devotion (bhakti) to a single deity over ritualism and caste distinctions.

• Nayanars came from various social backgrounds, including so-called lower castes.

NOTE

• Durga (Option 2): A fierce form of the mother goddess Shakti, worshipped especially during Navratri and Durga Puja.

• Agni (Option 3): The Vedic god of fire, one of the most invoked deities in the Rigveda.

• Indra (Option 4): The Vedic king of the gods and lord of thunder, rain and war.

question: Which article of the Indian Constitution mentions that There shall be a Comptroller and Auditor-General of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 148.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 148 of the Indian Constitution provides that there shall be a Comptroller and Auditor-General of India (भारत का नियंत्रक-महालेखापरीक्षक).

• The CAG is appointed by the President and can be removed only in the manner and on grounds prescribed for a judge of the Supreme Court.

• Articles 148 to 151 deal with the CAG — covering appointment, duties, powers and audit reports.

• The CAG is regarded as the guardian of the public purse and heads the Indian Audit and Accounts Department.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The salary and service conditions of the CAG are determined by Parliament and charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described the CAG as one of the most important officers under the Constitution.

• The CAG's audit reports are laid before Parliament and examined by the Public Accounts Committee (PAC).

NOTE

• Article 142 (Option 1): Empowers the Supreme Court to pass decrees necessary for doing complete justice.

• Article 144 (Option 2): Requires all civil and judicial authorities to act in aid of the Supreme Court.

• Article 146 (Option 3): Deals with officers, servants and expenses of the Supreme Court.

question: Which section of the Indian constitution ensure social and economic reforms in a country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Directive principal of state policy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (राज्य की नीति के निदेशक तत्व) aim to ensure social and economic reforms and establish a welfare state.

• They are contained in Part IV (Articles 36 to 51) of the Constitution and were borrowed from the Irish Constitution.

• They are non-justiciable, i.e., not enforceable by any court, but are fundamental in the governance of the country.

• They seek to secure social and economic justice by directing state policy on matters like equal pay, living wage and distribution of resources.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The DPSPs are classified broadly into Socialistic, Gandhian and Liberal-Intellectual principles.

• The state is expected to keep these principles in mind while framing laws and policies.

• The Minerva Mills case (1980) stressed a balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles.

NOTE

• Fundamental rights (Option 1): Justiciable rights in Part III (Articles 12–35) guaranteeing individual liberties.

• Fundamental duties (Option 2): Moral obligations of citizens in Part IV-A (Article 51A), added by the 42nd Amendment.

• Separation of powers (Option 3): A doctrine dividing powers among legislature, executive and judiciary, not a distinct section of the Constitution.

question: In July 2025, the 17th BRICS Summit was held in which of the following country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brazil.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 17th BRICS Summit was held in July 2025 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil (ब्राज़ील), under Brazil's chairship.

• BRICS is a grouping of major emerging economies; the name derives from Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa.

• The bloc has expanded to include new members such as Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE.

• India is scheduled to host the next (18th) BRICS Summit.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• BRICS established the New Development Bank (NDB), headquartered in Shanghai, China.

• The term 'BRIC' was coined by economist Jim O'Neill in 2001; South Africa joined in 2010.

• BRICS summits are held annually with a rotating chairship among members.

NOTE

• South Africa (Option 1): Hosted the 15th BRICS Summit in Johannesburg in 2023.

• Russia (Option 2): Hosted the 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan in 2024.

• India (Option 3): Will host the 18th BRICS Summit and previously hosted in 2012, 2016 and 2021.

question: The Asian Development Bank was founded in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1966.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Asian Development Bank (ADB) (एशियाई विकास बैंक) was founded in the year 1966.

• It is a regional development bank headquartered in Manila, Philippines.

• Its aim is to promote social and economic development in Asia and the Pacific region.

• It provides loans, technical assistance and grants to its member countries.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The ADB is modelled closely on the World Bank and has a weighted voting system.

• Its largest shareholders are Japan and the United States.

• India is a founding member and one of the largest borrowers of the ADB.

NOTE

• 1952 (Option 1): Not the founding year of the ADB.

• 1977 (Option 3): Not associated with the ADB's establishment.

• 1987 (Option 4): Not the founding year of the ADB.

question: Who was the first female teacher of India who founded the first girls' school?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Savitribai Jyotiba Phule.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Savitribai Jyotiba Phule (सावित्रीबाई ज्योतिबा फुले) is regarded as the first female teacher of India and a pioneer of women's education.

• Along with her husband Jyotirao Phule, she founded one of India's first girls' schools at Bhide Wada, Pune in 1848.

• She was a social reformer, poet and campaigner against caste and gender discrimination.

• Her birth anniversary, 3 January, is observed in her honour.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• She worked to educate women and marginalised communities and opposed practices like child marriage and sati.

• She and Jyotirao established the Satyashodhak Samaj to promote social equality.

• She died in 1897 while serving patients during a plague epidemic.

NOTE

• Annie Besant (Option 1): British-Indian theosophist and freedom fighter who founded the Home Rule League and Banaras Hindu College.

• Kasturba Gandhi (Option 2): Wife of Mahatma Gandhi and a freedom fighter who took part in various Satyagraha movements.

• Sarojini Naidu (Option 3): Poet and freedom fighter, the first Indian woman President of the Congress and first woman Governor of an Indian state.

question: Who was the first Indian to become WHO's Deputy Director General?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Soumya Swaminathan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr. Soumya Swaminathan (सौम्या स्वामीनाथन) was the first Indian to be appointed as the Deputy Director General of the World Health Organization (WHO).

• She is a paediatrician and clinical scientist known for her work on tuberculosis and HIV.

• She also served as the first Chief Scientist of the WHO.

• She is the daughter of Dr. M.S. Swaminathan, the father of India's Green Revolution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• She earlier headed the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) as Director General.

• She played a prominent role in guiding global health responses during the COVID-19 pandemic.

• The WHO is a specialised agency of the United Nations, headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

NOTE

• Chandrima Saha (Option 1): A biologist who became the first woman President of the Indian National Science Academy (INSA).

• Gagandeep Kang (Option 2): A noted vaccine scientist and the first Indian woman elected a Fellow of the Royal Society, London.

• Sanghamitra Bandyopadhyay (Option 3): A computer scientist and Director of the Indian Statistical Institute, known for work in bioinformatics.

question: In June 2025, who has been re-appointed as the new CBDT Chairman?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ravi Agarwal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In June 2025, Ravi Agarwal (रवि अग्रवाल) was re-appointed as the Chairman of the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT).

• The CBDT is a statutory authority functioning under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance.

• It is responsible for administering direct tax laws such as the Income Tax Act.

• His tenure was extended by re-appointment, reflecting continuity in tax administration.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The CBDT was constituted under the Central Board of Revenue Act, 1963.

• It provides essential inputs for policy and planning of direct taxes in India.

• The Board is headed by a Chairman and consists of several Members.

NOTE

• Anuj Kumar Singh (Option 2): Not associated with the CBDT Chairman post in this context.

• Rajiv Kumar (Option 3): Shares his name with a former Election Commissioner/Chief Election Commissioner of India.

• Sanjay Malhotra (Option 4): Was appointed Governor of the Reserve Bank of India in December 2024.

question: In July 2025, _____ was arrested in connection with the Andaman and Nicobar State Cooperative Bank Limited (ANSCBL) loan irregularities case.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kuldeep Sharma.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In July 2025, former Andaman and Nicobar MP Kuldeep Rai Sharma (कुलदीप शर्मा) was arrested by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) in the ANSCBL loan irregularities case.

• The case relates to alleged irregularities in loan sanctions of the Andaman and Nicobar State Cooperative Bank Limited (ANSCBL).

• The Enforcement Directorate (प्रवर्तन निदेशालय) probes money-laundering and foreign-exchange law violations.

• The ED acts under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Kuldeep Rai Sharma was a Congress leader who had represented the Andaman and Nicobar Islands in the Lok Sabha.

• The ED functions under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance.

• The case involved the ED's first-ever searches in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

NOTE

• Ashwani Gupta (Option 1): Not associated with the ANSCBL case in this context.

• Shashi Singh (Option 3): Not associated with the ANSCBL case in this context.

• Samir Shah (Option 4): Shares his name with the Chairman of the BBC, unrelated to this case.

question: In April 2025, Union Minister of Commerce & Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal announced that Second Fund of Funds for Startups worth Rs. _____ crore to boost deep-tech and early-stage innovation has been approved.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10000.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In April 2025, Commerce & Industry Minister Piyush Goyal announced the approval of a Second Fund of Funds for Startups (स्टार्टअप्स के लिए फंड ऑफ फंड्स) worth Rs. 10,000 crore.

• The fund is aimed at boosting deep-tech and early-stage innovation in India's startup ecosystem.

• A Fund of Funds does not invest directly in startups but into SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs).

• The move was announced under the framework of the Startup India initiative.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The first Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS) of Rs. 10,000 crore was announced in 2016, managed by SIDBI.

• The Union Budget 2025-26 had proposed a new Fund of Funds with an expanded scope.

• Startup India was launched in January 2016 to promote entrepreneurship and innovation.

NOTE

• 5000 (Option 2): Not the announced corpus for the Second Fund of Funds.

• 8000 (Option 3): Not the announced corpus for the Second Fund of Funds.

• 3000 (Option 4): Not the announced corpus for the Second Fund of Funds.

question: In the Union Budget 2025-26, there has been a plan establish _____ Day Care Cancer Centres in 2025-26.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 200.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Union Budget 2025-26 (केंद्रीय बजट 2025-26) proposed setting up 200 Day Care Cancer Centres in district hospitals in the year 2025-26.

• The Budget planned to establish day care cancer centres in all district hospitals over the next three years.

• The scheme aims to improve access to cancer treatment such as chemotherapy closer to patients' homes.

• The Budget was presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Budget also exempted several life-saving cancer and rare-disease drugs from basic customs duty.

• It proposed adding 10,000 additional seats in medical colleges.

• Healthcare and medical education received strong emphasis in the 2025-26 Budget.

NOTE

• 500 (Option 2): Not the number of centres planned for 2025-26.

• 350 (Option 3): Not the number of centres planned for 2025-26.

• 750 (Option 4): Not the number of centres planned for 2025-26.

question: National Infrastructure Readiness Index (NIRI) was launched in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is September 2024.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Infrastructure Readiness Index (NIRI) (राष्ट्रीय अवसंरचना तत्परता सूचकांक) was launched in September 2024.

• It is designed to assess and monitor the readiness of infrastructure projects across the country.

• The index helps in tracking infrastructure development and identifying bottlenecks.

• It supports data-driven decision making in the infrastructure sector.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India has been pushing large-scale infrastructure growth through initiatives like the National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP) and PM Gati Shakti.

• Infrastructure development is seen as key to India's goal of becoming a developed nation.

• Such indices aid transparency and accountability in project execution.

NOTE

• April 2024 (Option 2): Not the launch month of the NIRI.

• August 2025 (Option 3): Not the launch month of the NIRI.

• January 2025 (Option 4): Not the launch month of the NIRI.

question: First Asian Games were held at _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is New Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first Asian Games (प्रथम एशियाई खेल) were held in New Delhi, India in 1951.

• They were hosted at the National Stadium (Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium) in New Delhi.

• The Asian Games are a continental multi-sport event held every four years.

• The Games are governed by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India also hosted the Asian Games in 1982 in New Delhi.

• The idea of the Asian Games was promoted by Prof. G.D. Sondhi.

• The motto of the Asian Games is 'Ever Onward'.

NOTE

• Tokyo (Option 2): Japan hosted the Asian Games in 1958; Tokyo also hosted the Summer Olympics in 1964 and 2021.

• Beijing (Option 3): China hosted the Asian Games in 1990 and 2010 (Guangzhou); Beijing hosted the 2008 Olympics.

• Jakarta (Option 4): Indonesia's Jakarta hosted the Asian Games in 1962 and 2018.

question: National Swimming Association of India was founded in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1949.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Swimming Association of India / Swimming Federation of India (भारतीय राष्ट्रीय तैराकी संघ) was founded in the year 1949.

• It is the governing body for the sport of swimming and aquatics in India.

• It regulates competitive swimming, diving and water polo in the country.

• It is affiliated to the international and Asian aquatics federations.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The body organises national swimming championships across various age categories.

• Swimming is a core discipline in the Olympics, Asian Games and Commonwealth Games.

• India's swimmers compete under this federation at international events.

NOTE

• 1955 (Option 1): Not the founding year of the association.

• 1953 (Option 2): Not the founding year of the association.

• 1947 (Option 4): The year of India's independence, not the founding year of the association.

question: In July 2025, the National Green Tribunal has imposed a total fine of Rs. 23.7 crore on authorities in _____ over green belt pollution.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In July 2025, the National Green Tribunal (NGT) (राष्ट्रीय हरित न्यायाधिकरण) imposed a total fine of Rs. 23.7 crore on authorities in Uttar Pradesh over green belt pollution.

• The NGT is a specialised judicial body for effective and speedy disposal of environmental cases.

• It was established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.

• Its principal bench is located in New Delhi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The NGT follows the principles of natural justice and is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure.

• It applies principles such as sustainable development, the precautionary principle and the polluter pays principle.

• India was among the first countries to set up a dedicated environmental tribunal.

NOTE

• Bihar (Option 2): Not the state where the fine was imposed in this case.

• Jharkhand (Option 3): Not the state where the fine was imposed in this case.

• Gujarat (Option 4): Not the state where the fine was imposed in this case.

question: Gymnastics Federation of India was established in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1951.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Gymnastics Federation of India (GFI) (जिम्नास्टिक फेडरेशन ऑफ इंडिया) was established in the year 1951.

• It is the national governing body for the sport of gymnastics in India.

• It organises national gymnastics championships and selects athletes for international events.

• It works to promote and develop gymnastics across the country.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Gymnastics includes disciplines such as artistic, rhythmic and trampoline gymnastics.

• Dipa Karmakar became the first Indian female gymnast to qualify for the Olympics (Rio 2016).

• Gymnastics is a regular event at the Olympics, Asian Games and Commonwealth Games.

NOTE

• 1947 (Option 1): The year of India's independence, not the founding year of the GFI.

• 1948 (Option 2): Not the founding year of the GFI.

• 1953 (Option 4): Not the founding year of the GFI.

question: Salkhan Fossil Park is in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Salkhan Fossil Park (सलखन जीवाश्म पार्क) is located in the Sonbhadra district of Uttar Pradesh.

• It is famous for its ancient stromatolite fossils, estimated to be around 1.4 billion years old.

• These fossils are among the oldest records of life on Earth.

• The park has been added to the UNESCO World Heritage tentative list.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Stromatolites are layered structures formed by the activity of cyanobacteria (blue-green algae).

• The park is considered older and richer in some respects than fossil sites like Yellowstone in the USA.

• Sonbhadra is often called the 'energy capital' of India due to its power plants and mineral resources.

NOTE

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 2): Home to the Ghughua Fossil Park (Dindori), not Salkhan.

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 3): Not the location of Salkhan Fossil Park.

• Kerala (Option 4): Not the location of Salkhan Fossil Park.

question: In _____ 2026, World Athletics Cross Country Championships will be held in USA.
solution_text:
The correct answer is January.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The World Athletics Cross Country Championships (विश्व एथलेटिक्स क्रॉस कंट्री चैंपियनशिप) will be held in January 2026 in the USA.

• It is one of the premier long-distance running competitions in the world.

• The event is organised by World Athletics, the global governing body for athletics.

• The championships bring together elite distance runners from across the globe.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• World Athletics was formerly known as the International Association of Athletics Federations (IAAF).

• The body is headquartered in Monaco.

• Cross country running takes place over natural terrain such as grass and mud.

NOTE

• March (Option 2): Not the scheduled month for the 2026 championships.

• April (Option 3): Not the scheduled month for the 2026 championships.

• July (Option 4): Not the scheduled month for the 2026 championships.

question: What important event is celebrated during the festival of 'Baisakhi' in Chandigarh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Founding of Khalsa Panth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• During the festival of Baisakhi (बैसाखी), the founding of the Khalsa Panth (खालसा पंथ की स्थापना) by Guru Gobind Singh in 1699 is commemorated.

• Baisakhi is celebrated mainly in Punjab and neighbouring regions like Chandigarh.

• It also marks the harvest of the Rabi crop and the Punjabi/Sikh New Year.

• It usually falls on 13 or 14 April every year.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Guru Gobind Singh was the tenth Sikh Guru and founded the Khalsa at Anandpur Sahib.

• The Panj Pyare (Five Beloved Ones) were the first members initiated into the Khalsa.

• Baisakhi is celebrated with fairs, folk dances like Bhangra and Gidda, and visits to gurdwaras.

NOTE

• Birth of Guru Nanak (Option 1): Celebrated as Guru Nanak Jayanti (Gurpurab), usually in November.

• Founding of Golden Temple (Option 2): The Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib) in Amritsar is associated with Guru Arjan Dev, not Baisakhi.

• Birth of Guru Angad (Option 3): Guru Angad Dev was the second Sikh Guru; his birth is observed separately, not on Baisakhi.

question: Which of the following was the aim of Liberalisation under New Economic Policy 1991 of India?
option_1: To put embargo on enemy countries trade.
option_2: To increase restrictions on economic activities.
option_3: To open various sector of the economy.
option_4: To increase non-tariff barrier on Imports.
solution_text:
The correct answer is To open various sector of the economy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The aim of Liberalisation (उदारीकरण) under the New Economic Policy of 1991 was to open various sectors of the economy and reduce government controls.

• It sought to end the 'Licence-Permit-Quota Raj' and give a greater role to the private sector.

• The reforms are often summarised by the acronym LPG — Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation.

• They were introduced in response to a severe balance of payments crisis in 1991.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The reforms were introduced under PM P.V. Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh.

• Liberalisation reduced industrial licensing, lowered tariffs and eased restrictions on foreign investment.

• The reforms marked a shift from a controlled economy towards a market-oriented economy.

NOTE

• To put embargo on enemy countries trade (Option 1): An embargo is a trade ban, which is the opposite of liberalisation.

• To increase restrictions on economic activities (Option 2): Liberalisation reduced, not increased, economic restrictions.

• To increase non-tariff barrier on Imports (Option 4): Liberalisation aimed to lower trade barriers, not raise them.

question: Which of the following was the British East India Company's first major victory in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Battle of Plassey.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Battle of Plassey (प्लासी की लड़ाई), fought in 1757, was the British East India Company's first major victory in India.

• It was fought between the forces of Robert Clive and Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah of Bengal.

• The British victory was aided by the betrayal of the Nawab's commander Mir Jafar.

• It laid the foundation of British political power in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• After Plassey, Mir Jafar was installed as the puppet Nawab of Bengal.

• The Battle of Buxar (1764) further consolidated British control over Bengal, Bihar and Odisha.

• Plassey is located in present-day West Bengal.

NOTE

• Battle of Ambur (Option 1): Fought in 1749 during the Second Carnatic War between rival claimants backed by the French and British.

• Battle of Wandiwash (Option 2): Fought in 1760, a decisive British victory over the French in the Third Carnatic War.

• First Anglo-Maratha war (Option 3): Fought between 1775 and 1782, ending with the Treaty of Salbai.

question: Which bill/act provided for the trial of British or European persons by Indians, and sought equality between British and Indian judges?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ilbert Bill of 1883.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Ilbert Bill of 1883 (इल्बर्ट बिल 1883) proposed to allow Indian judges to try British or European persons, seeking equality between British and Indian judges.

• It was introduced during the viceroyalty of Lord Ripon and drafted by Sir Courtenay Ilbert.

• The bill faced strong opposition from the European community in India.

• Due to this protest, the bill was heavily diluted before being passed.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The controversy exposed the racial bias of British rule and stirred Indian nationalist feeling.

• It is often seen as one of the factors leading to the founding of the Indian National Congress in 1885.

• Lord Ripon is also remembered for the Resolution on Local Self-Government (1882).

NOTE

• Regulating Act of 1773 (Option 1): First major British Act to regulate the East India Company, creating the post of Governor-General of Bengal.

• Pitt's India Act of 1784 (Option 3): Established the Board of Control, introducing dual control over Indian affairs.

• Indian Councils Act of 1892 (Option 4): Enlarged the legislative councils and introduced a limited, indirect element of election.

question: In 1991, rupee was devalued in two stages and the cumulative devaluation was about _____ percent in USD terms.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 18.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 1991, the Indian rupee was devalued (अवमूल्यन) in two stages, with a cumulative devaluation of about 18 percent in USD terms.

• The devaluation took place amid a severe balance of payments crisis.

• It was carried out by the Reserve Bank of India in July 1991.

• The aim was to make Indian exports more competitive and correct the external imbalance.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• During the 1991 crisis, India had to pledge its gold reserves to raise foreign exchange.

• The devaluation coincided with the launch of the LPG economic reforms.

• P.V. Narasimha Rao was the Prime Minister and Manmohan Singh the Finance Minister at the time.

NOTE

• 28 (Option 2): Not the approximate cumulative devaluation figure.

• 32 (Option 3): Not the approximate cumulative devaluation figure.

• 36 (Option 4): Not the approximate cumulative devaluation figure.

question: Which of the following Indian states does not have a Legislative Council?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Among the given options, Rajasthan (राजस्थान) does not have a Legislative Council (विधान परिषद्); it has only a Legislative Assembly.

• A Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) is the upper house of a state legislature.

• Only a few Indian states have a bicameral legislature with a Legislative Council.

• The council is a permanent house and is not subject to dissolution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Under Article 169, Parliament can create or abolish a Legislative Council on a resolution passed by the concerned state assembly.

• States with a Legislative Council include Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.

• One-third of the council members retire every two years.

NOTE

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 1): Has a Legislative Council and is a bicameral state legislature.

• Bihar (Option 2): Has a Legislative Council and a bicameral legislature.

• Maharashtra (Option 4): Has a Legislative Council and a bicameral legislature.

question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding the article 253 of Indian Constitution?
I. It is found in Part XI of the Constitution.
II. It relates to the Legislation for giving effect to international agreements.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 253 (अनुच्छेद 253) of the Indian Constitution deals with Legislation for giving effect to international agreements, so statement II is correct.

• Article 253 is placed in Part XI (Relations between the Union and the States), so statement I is also correct.

• It empowers Parliament to make laws for the whole or any part of India to implement any treaty, agreement or convention with other countries.

• Hence both statements are correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Part XI (Articles 245–263) deals with legislative and administrative relations between the Union and the States.

• Article 253 allows Parliament to legislate even on State List subjects to fulfil international obligations.

• This provision reflects the supremacy of the Union in matters of international agreements.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, as statement II regarding international agreements is also correct.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete, as statement I regarding Part XI is also correct.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, as both statements are actually true.
